# Plan: SDK quickstart docs

## Onboarding flow
Step 1: clone the repo.
Step 2: install bun manually if not present.
Step 3: copy .env.example to .env and fill in 8 environment variables.
Step 4: run database migrations against your local Postgres.
Step 5: start the dev server.
Step 6: open the docs in a separate tab.
Step 7: register an API key by emailing the team.
Step 8: paste the key into your .env, restart the server, then make
your first SDK call.

No quickstart command, no hosted sandbox, no copy-pasteable curl example.

question.question:
D2 — Which time-to-first-call target should this quickstart be reviewed against?
Project/branch/task: main branch, /plan-devex-review of PLAN.md, DX POLISH mode with product scope held.
ELI10: For a hands-on developer on a fresh machine, going from opening the quickstart to a first SDK call takes an estimated 25-60 minutes of active work (8 steps) plus an unknown wait for a key emailed by your team. Peers like Stripe are reported under 5 minutes because the key is self-serve and nothing runs locally; that comparison is on DX choices, not equal time boundaries. The target you pick is what Pass 1 and Pass 8 will score the plan against.
Stakes if we pick wrong: pick too ambitious and the review demands scope you've said to hold; pick too loose and the report blesses a journey that category evidence says loses 50-70% of developers past 10 minutes.
Recommendation: C because Champion and Competitive both require removing the email-a-human key step and the local Postgres requirement, which are product changes outside DX POLISH scope; C keeps them visible as out-of-scope opportunities while polishing every touchpoint of the declared journey.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=4/10, D=depends on your answer
Pros / cons:
A) Champion (< 2 min)
  ✅ Matches the DX choices of the best-known SDK onboarding flows in the category
  ✅ Forces the quickstart to lead with one copy-paste call and a self-serve key
  ❌ Not reachable within the declared journey: requires a hosted sandbox or self-serve key, both new scope. Blockers: steps 1-4 and 7 all have to go.
B) Competitive (2-5 min)
  ✅ Still a self-contained first call with no human in the loop
  ✅ Gives a clear line for what the docs must cut versus what they can explain
  ❌ Also requires self-serve keys and no local database, which are product decisions currently undecided. Blockers: steps 4 and 7.
C) Current trajectory, polished (est. 25-60 min active + unknown key wait) (recommended)
  ✅ Feasible inside DX POLISH: every one of the 8 steps gets prerequisites, commands, expected output, and error guidance
  ✅ Keeps the review honest: the report records the measured gap to peers and lists self-serve key and no-local-DB as out-of-scope opportunities
  ❌ Stays in the >10 minute tier by category benchmarks; polishing cannot remove the email wait. Blocker: turnaround time is unmeasured.
D) Tell me what's realistic
  ✅ You know the real key turnaround and whether Postgres is truly required for a first call
  ✅ Lets you set a target that reflects roadmap intent rather than benchmark tiers
  ❌ Delays the trace until you answer; an unlabeled estimate would weaken the report
Net: A and B are where the category is; C is the only target the held scope can actually reach, so the trade is honest gap reporting versus reopening product scope.

D2 — Which TTHW target should this review measure the quickstart against?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-jpwMXb on main, /plan-devex-review of PLAN.md, DX POLISH mode.
ELI10: TTHW is time to hello world: how long from reading Step 1 until the first SDK call returns something the developer understands. For a hands-on dev making a first call, the 8 declared steps come to roughly 20-45 minutes of active work (estimated, not measured), plus an unbounded wait at Step 7 because the API key arrives by email. Peers (Stripe, Twilio) are reported at 2-5 minutes from a hosted signup, which is a different starting line, so the comparison is directional. The target you pick is the bar every later pass scores against. It does not approve any fix; remedies stay pending.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too ambitious and every pass flags out-of-scope work; too lax and the review blesses a flow that benchmarks predict 50-70% of developers abandon.
Recommendation: B because 2-5 minutes is where SDK first-call peers sit and it is the bar your persona arrives with; note that docs polish alone cannot reach it while Steps 4 and 7 stay on the critical path, so expect out-of-scope opportunities listed separately.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10, D=n/a
Pros / cons:
A) Champion (< 2 min)
  ✅ Matches the 3-4x adoption uplift tier and forces the sharpest possible quickstart
  ✅ Makes every remaining friction point visible as a measurable gap in the report
  ❌ Not reachable without a hosted sandbox or self-serve keys, both outside the supplied docs scope
B) Competitive (2-5 min) (recommended)
  ✅ Same tier as Stripe and Twilio's reported first-call times, the bar this persona expects
  ✅ Reachable in principle if key issuance and DB setup leave the critical path; docs-only fixes still narrow the gap
  ❌ Blockers are Step 7 (emailed key, unknown turnaround) and Step 4 (local Postgres); removing either is a separate scope decision
C) Current trajectory (~20-45 min active + unbounded wait)
  ✅ Honest about what docs polish alone can deliver inside the current 8-step flow
  ✅ No out-of-scope pressure; the review focuses purely on clarity of each existing step
  ❌ Accepts a Red Flag tier (>10 min) as the goal, which benchmarks associate with 50-70% abandonment
D) Tell me what's realistic
  ✅ You know key turnaround and infra constraints I cannot see from the plan
  ✅ Lets the target reflect a measured or known number instead of my estimate
  ❌ Needs your typed number now; nothing proceeds until it lands
Net: pick the bar; whether Steps 4 and 7 get reworked to meet it is decided separately, one question at a time.
